title: Capitolo 3 · Verbs, the time and free time
shortDescription: The present tense of regular verbs in -ARE, -ERE and -IRE, negative sentences with NON, the most important irregular verbs, telling the time, hobbies and sports, how often you do things and what you like.
description:
Part of the official SS Europa Italian course used in our classes, for learners from India, Pakistan and Bangladesh who are going to Italy to work, study or live. Chapters 1–7 take you from zero to level A1 and Chapters 8–12 to level A2 — study them in order.

Every 60-minute class of the chapter is split into three short lessons you can study on your phone, with pictures, audio, grammar tables and exercises. Every word comes with its English and Punjabi meaning, the slides of each class are attached as PDF, and the chapter ends with a test (pass mark 60%).
objectives:
I can use regular verbs in -ARE, -ERE and -IRE in the present tense
I can build a sentence and make it negative with NON
I can use irregular verbs: andare, fare, stare, bere, volere, potere, dovere, venire, uscire…
I can ask and tell the time and say when I do things
I can talk about my hobbies and how often I do them
I can say what I like and don't like with mi piace / mi piacciono

blocks.body:

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: **-ISC-** goes in io, tu, lui/lei and loro, but **not in noi and voi**: *capisco, capisci, capisce, capiamo, capite, capiscono*. In **-sco** and **-scono** the sound is hard [sk]; in **-sci** and **-sce** it is soft [sh].

Io ascolto sempre la musica. · Lui va spesso in palestra.
Io non lavoro mai la domenica. · Noi non beviamo mai vino.
qualche volta → at the start or at the end
Qualche volta vado al cinema. · Vado al cinema qualche volta.

blocks.title: Test Capitolo 3
blocks.body:
This test checks everything in Chapter 3 (Lessons 1–4).

- **1. Listening** — sentences and times
- **2. Vocabulary** — free time, sports, frequency and the time
- **3. Grammar** — regular and irregular verbs, NON, mi piace / mi piacciono
- **4. Writing** — sentences about your day

You need **60%** to pass. You can repeat the test as many times as you like.
